P1.evidence: Setter notes used twice and used well — 'I already heard a few things from Derek', then later 'I already heard something from Derek around that sense that you're not 100% happy with [mobility]', which opened the mobility thread. Frame was three-part again — 'where you're at, where you want to go, make sure we really fit in there' — missing what's in the way and what you need. Agreement asked and given ('Sounds good? Sounds good. Yep'), and the standard open question ran.

P2.evidence: The injury probe was the best-run check on the call — the rep asked for severity on a 1-to-10 scale and for duration, and got a precise answer ('For 20 years, back issues were severe probably for like a total of a month'). Diet was properly probed, including pushing on 'for the most part' to get the cheat frequency. Age was asked directly (45); height was never asked and weight was volunteered. Work was never asked at all — the prospect mentioned 'sitting at a desk all day' and the rep did not follow up, so his occupation is unknown, which also means the primary ICP criterion went untested. Health conditions, sleep and energy were all skipped entirely.

P3.evidence: The rep did reach for the bridge, twice — 'What got you to be like, you know what, I'm gonna jump on a meeting with these guys?' and 'What was that switch for you to be like, I'm actually going to take it more serious again now?' — and got nothing back: 'Nothing specific... now is as good a time as'. The failure is what came next. Instead of digging, he ratified the emptiness out loud: 'you're quite straightforward... There's no big reason behind it. You just want to go for it now.' Nobody else was ever brought into the frame, no legacy, identity or longevity thread was pulled, and no reflect-back was attempted. The six-month success question ran but produced only 'physical form should be better, lower body fat, muscular physique. That's it.' The call then priced against a prospect with no stated why, which is the direct cause of the think-about-it.

P4.evidence: Training history was collected but never interrogated as a set of failed attempts. This prospect self-described twenty years of on-and-off training with repeated three-to-four-month lapses — the root-cause question writes itself and was never asked. Worse, the rep supplied the gap himself rather than letting the prospect name it: 'you can keep training on and off the whole time, but eventually those small inconsistencies, they will blow up again.' P4f is the single most relevant check on this call for a capable, self-directed lifter already getting results from free videos, and it was not asked.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The closest thing is a rep assertion — 'those small inconsistencies, they will blow up again, they will go away, they will blow up again' — delivered as a statement, not asked as a question, and never landed on the prospect. There is no two-year picture, no willing-to-settle test and no line in the sand anywhere in the transcript. When the price objection arrived the playbook says return to Phase 5; there was no Phase 5 to return to.

P6.evidence: P6b ran cleanly — 'do you feel like when it comes to the training, mobility, nutrition, and that lifelong success part with Trevor, that there would be any reason that you're not going to be able to get to...' answered 'No. I mean, it's pretty straightforward.' But belief in needing the structure was never tested, and P6c failed twice over: the prospect had already flagged cost as the deciding factor six minutes before price ('if money was no object, this would be no question'), and when hesitation duly surfaced the rep did not return to Phase 5 — he cut the price in half instead.

P11.evidence: No agreement on either tier, so payment and onboarding were never reachable. Nothing was sent, nothing was booked, and the rep did not even secure a follow-up call — he accepted 'I'll get back to you within the next two days'.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:20:56, verbatim 'I need to still think about it'. Two moves ran, and ran well: the isolation, 'Outside of the investment, do you feel like, yes, I do want to do this?', and the value test, 'Do you feel like that is worth 6K to you?' The rest of the play was abandoned — no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here, when do you make a different decision', no closing 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. The prospect's answer to the isolation was diagnostic gold — 'It's not how, it's just a matter of deciding if I should' — which says the blocker is conviction, not money, and the rep responded by discounting.

Trigger at 00:22:52, '6,000 is a lot of money... we're not all millionaires here'. Exactly one financial-picture question ran — 'So what do you feel like you would even have available' — answered 'I don't know yet' and dropped. None of the rest: no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments, and critically no 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' — a payment plan was never offered on this call at all. Instead the rep introduced an undisclosed $3,000 tier with a different coach. Note also that OC was arguably the wrong play: the prospect had just told him it was a should-I question, not a how question, which points to OA and value, not to capacity.

Script gap, and the same one already logged from the Badrane Hriouch call: a cheaper alternative the prospect believes will work. Here it is in-person personal training at his own gym — 'it's a little more accessible when I go to the gym' — plus the free online kettlebell videos that have already produced visible results for him in two weeks. He even handed over the counter-argument himself, 'obviously people are not as much of a kettlebell expert', and the rep never picked it up. There is no scripted play for defending a premium against a functioning low-cost substitute, and this call needed one.
No spouse or partner consult raised; no family situation was ever established.
No timing objection — he volunteered the opposite: 'there's never not a good time to do it'.
No fear or doubt about the programme working. His injury concern is a reason to buy, not a doubt, and the rep used it correctly as such.

notes: The rep asked the right bridge questions, got nothing, and then told the prospect out loud that there was no big reason behind it — which removed the only leverage the call had. With no why, no root cause and no consequence frame, $6,000 arrived naked and predictably bounced. The coaching priority is what happened next: a half-price tier with a different coach appeared within ninety seconds of the first objection, before a payment plan was ever offered and before the OA play was finished. Discounting to a value objection teaches the prospect the price is negotiable and re-anchors him at $3,000. Finish OA, offer the payment split, and only then consider tier changes — and never before establishing what the prospect actually does for a living.
